scope: Fresh exact-input bounded SOG JSON cleanup authority, compatibility fallback, retained native stream/export/census contracts, affected browser paths, production compatibility/initialization and the identified unit run. Counts are intentionally not added across overlapping runs.

censusQualification: scoped-cxx-v1 observes tagged admitted payload and raw C++ blocks including setup contexts. Raw C codec allocation, malloc fragmentation, exception ABI storage, MEMFS JS buffers and GPU memory are excluded. No new admission credit or quota enforcement. The final native fixture intentionally retains a loaded two-vertex PLY: actual payload/overlap32 and raw union845. Twenty ordinary refusals are four repetitions each of null open, small ResourceBudget open, malformed ASCII PLY open, unsupported export and null command; backend injections are separately counted and do not establish arbitrary mid-mutation failure atomicity.
cleanupQualification: The actual adapted SPZ library closes 37 successfully initialized zlib streams and 103 observed raw codec blocks across successful, ordinary-error, initialization-refusal and throwing-vector paths. Two reserve/two insert case counters exclude eight extra repeated insert refusals with successful recoveries. Export exercises all eight supported format IDs, 130 filesystem refusals, two invalid requests, one candidate-vector refusal and 24 successes. Actual output pointer/bytes, scene owner/records, mask owner/bytes, full summary, census, private files/streams and executable Redo are checked; one successful nested-request CSV boundary has zero observed C++ allocation attempts/backend events after output publication; this does not observe all raw C or JS allocation. Target-only controls are absent from shipping assets. Close-error probes report failure after the wrapper retires the read descriptor, and do not qualify failure before descriptor retirement. No raw codec quota, MEMFS credit, arbitrary JSON/command-wide closed-refusal guarantee or arbitrary unlink-failure cleanup is established.
responseAllocationQualification: 136 observed operator-new boundaries in the linked response contracts; request parsing, exception construction, arbitrary malloc and whole-operation allocation are outside that observation. The 16549-byte response reserve belongs to measured heap H, not scene C.
jsonCleanupQualification: A fixed-array, allocation-free UTF-8/JSON scanner qualifies only the exact borrowed SOG metadata bytes within default byte/depth/token/decoded-string/numeric bounds. A noncopyable parsed owner keeps its private thread-local authority active through parse temporaries and DOM destruction, restoring or masking nested authority. Qualified paths use bounded recursive destruction with no heap flatten stack; unqualified inputs retain the original parser and iterative destructor without new rejection. Shipping and contract JSON translation units share the generated header. The native owner and actual bundled candidate allocation sweeps observe no C++ new/backend events after injected refusal through their observed unwind boundaries. Successful content-key formatting uses fixed digest/hex arrays followed by one throwing owning-string allocation; an independent hashlib ZIP digest checks successful output. This is not a whole-operation quota or generic command refusal guarantee.
jsonCleanupLimitations: Qualification limits select destruction behavior; they are not new acceptance limits or admission credit.
Unqualified fallback retains its original potentially allocating destructor; fallback cleanup allocation failure is not injected or qualified.
Sampled destructor stack-pointer deltas are a regression observation, not exhaustive high-water measurement or a universal stack bound.
Separate SourceSnapshot preparses, request/live-preview DOMs and constructed export DOMs remain unqualified.
Observations cover scoped C++ allocation events, excluding raw C codecs, exception ABI, JavaScript/MEMFS and GPU memory.
cleanupLimitations: SPZ cleanup qualifies legacy gzip v2/v3 paths, not v4/Zstd; low-level SPZ output may be cleared or partially filled on refusal.
Unlink itself is not faulted; AtomicFile attempts removal and ignores its error code.
The close-error wrapper closes the descriptor before reporting failure; failure before retirement is unqualified.
Private-file creation refusal, oversized output and postpublication allocation observation are CSV-only cases.
Header framing and deterministic retries do not independently decode every exported format.
